blocks.name: items
blocks.why: web_search retrieves current mid-market prices, supplier geography, and availability for process materials. Coverage is partial because web_search returns useful data for widely-traded ingredients but has no source for obscure, novel, or proprietary materials — in those cases unit_cost must be null and a note is required. The partial stamp admits unavailable_no_tool_source as a valid provenance verdict, which is exactly what happens when an ingredient is not traceable to a public market. cost_low, cost_high, and source_region are sourced from the same search; scro_class is not sourced — see the risks block.

blocks.name: risks

source.from: items + domain knowledge of supply chain geography, seasonality, and adulteration patterns

blocks.why: Risk assessment is model inference over the items block, grounded in domain knowledge about supplier geography (single_source, geopolitical), harvest windows (seasonal), batch variation (quality_variable), current supply constraints (supply_tight), and adulteration patterns (substitution_risk). No tool lookup supplies risk flags — they are the agent's reasoned judgement about each item's supply chain disposition. scro_class is also inferred here: the agent classifies each item into the closest SCRO continuant class (BiologicalMaterial, IndustrialChemical, etc.) from training knowledge of SCRO, not from a retrieval. Stamped model_inference so no run can present a reasoned risk assessment as a retrieved fact.

blocks.name: summary
blocks.why: total_bom_cost is arithmetic over the items block — it multiplies each item's unit_cost by its requested quantity (from the BomQuery) and sums. This is a computation the agent does over retrieved values, not a retrieval itself. oracle_note is the agent's single most important supply chain observation synthesised across the full BoM — it is the one place where a cross-item pattern (portfolio-level risk, dominant cost driver, substitution opportunity) that no individual item block captures can be surfaced. Both fields are model judgements.
